hero.leadBold: I solve complex problems and turn ambitious ideas into useful products, strategies and action.
hero.leadBody: Good outcomes begin with clear thinking. AI has shortened the distance between an idea and something real, but speed has only made the right questions more important. I look beneath the obvious problem, challenge what others take for granted and use the best tools available to move from sound judgement to purposeful action.
hero.proofLine: I use AI to build real products, like BumpNotes and Big Picture Planner. Now I help founders, health teams and organisations build their own.

equity.heading: I take hard problems and turn them into something useful.
equity.intro: Here are a few examples from outside my clinical work. I help more people from underrepresented backgrounds get into medicine. I also share health information people can trust with their communities.

cards.title: Trustee, WPMN
cards.body: An active trustee with the Widening Participation Medics Network, helping open a career in medicine to people who’d rarely picture it as theirs.

cards.title: CAHN Health Hour
cards.body: I’ve hosted and spoken for the Caribbean & African Health Network, sharing health knowledge people can use.

cards.title: “It’s All Gone Tits Up”
cards.body: I supported a breast cancer screening campaign that encouraged women to get screened early.

projectsSection.heading: Every project begins with a problem worth solving.
projectsSection.intro: I built most of what you see here myself. I use AI tools like Lovable, Claude Code and ChatGPT to go from an idea to a live product in days. GA4 and Microsoft Clarity keep me honest about what’s actually working.

bumpnotes.problem: Pregnancy information is fragmented, and the details that matter are hard to recall under pressure.
bumpnotes.built: A patient-owned pregnancy record that helps women capture what matters, in their own words.
bumpnotes.changed: Women get a simple record they can actually use, and a summary they can share when it counts.
bumpnotes.shows: Product thinking, real healthcare context, and technology built responsibly.

bigPicturePlanner.problem: Traditional planners reward busyness and let urgent tasks crowd out what actually matters.
bigPicturePlanner.built: A weekly planning system built around a whole week, not just a to-do list.
bigPicturePlanner.changed: People can see the bigger picture and still know their next practical step.
bigPicturePlanner.shows: Product thinking applied to a problem I lived myself.

mybishbash.problem: Phones are designed to capture attention, even when that fights the life someone actually wants.
mybishbash.built: An intentional phone app that replaces restriction and guilt with deliberate choices.
mybishbash.changed: People shape their phone use around their own priorities, calmly.
mybishbash.shows: Building for behaviour change, not just features.
